date: 11 Dec 1513 (626, "Ex Turegho xi x.bris") and May 1514 (636)
title: Two glossed letters of 1513-14 in letter-and-figure cipher with interlinear decipherment: a Medici agent with the Swiss (Zurich) and "Raffaello ..." (Rome? 1514)
correspondents: 626: an agent at Zurich (signature read by the pager as "S.tor ... Ghorus?") -> Lorenzo di Piero de' Medici; 636: Raffaello [surname not read] -> a Medici patron
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, docs. 626 (cc. 634-634 bis) and 636 (c. 644)
folio_note: 626 c. 634r: 4 cipher lines in the middle (lower-case letters, digits 2-9, H, KK, superscript indices) with interlinear clear text in a second hand ("io ho ricercato cinque cantoni de suizeri"); c. 634v: about 10 lines, glossed (Swiss, the Catholic king, the emperor, the king of England); c. 634 bis r: one glossed line. 636 c. 644r: about 16 lines in two blocks, glossed (the king of England, the Swiss); c. 644v: about 7 glossed lines.
why: Plaintext-aligned examples of the 1513-14 superscript-index ciphers: the first test for the bare Corsi letters and the Guicciardini letter (rows), and for the MAP LXXII 1513-15 family.
verify: Record the sign/letter pairs of each and compare the tables with each other and with the Corsi ciphertext.

date: undated (late 15th or early 16th century; names Orlando Pallavicino, Parma, Cremona?, Ferrara, Venice)
title: Two small code-word lists (numbered cover words and signs for persons and places), undated, unattributed
correspondents: unknown (Medici chancery or an agent); no address
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, docs. 1053 (old nos. 643/551) and 1054 (old nos. 152/408)
folio_note: 1053 r: a grid of 20 numbered entries, each a meaning above a cover word ("Lorenzo" 1, "la guerra"/"la nebia" 5, "el papa"/"el fratello" 12, "la pratica"/"la fine" 18; "messer Pallo" 20?), some struck through. 1054 r: about 22 entries, a name or term ("Vinegia", "Firenze", "Cardinale", "Orlando Palavicino", "Parma") with a cover word below and a sign or number under each (3, 9, p, m, b, f, kh, L, then 1-22); 1054 v: two or three more entries.
status: Key lists (1341-1411 px); not matched to any letter.
why: Two small nomenclators of cover words: keys for jargon letters (cover words in clear text) rather than for sign cipher; a date from the names would place them (an Orlando Pallavicino is active under the Ambrosian Republic, 1447-50, and another c. 1500).
verify: Transcribe both lists; date from the persons named; search MAP for letters using the cover words ("la nebia", "el fratello", "la fine").
